references.text: David asks that the Lord's face may shine upon him, reflecting the blessing that the Lord lifts his face toward his people.
The psalm asks that God may let his face shine upon the people, a direct parallel to the Aaronic blessing.
The Lord blesses his people with peace (shalom), the same blessing that concludes the Aaronic blessing.
God speaks peace to his people, connecting to the promise of shalom in the blessing.
The Lord keeps in perfect peace the one who trusts in him, an elaboration of the shalom blessing.
The Messiah is called the Prince of Peace, and his kingdom of peace shall have no end - a fulfillment of the shalom promise.
God promises to establish a covenant of peace with his people, expanding on the meaning of divine peace.
Jesus gives his peace to the disciples, a peace that surpasses the world's peace - fulfillment of the shalom blessing.
The risen Jesus greets the disciples with 'Peace be with you', reflecting the conclusion of the Aaronic blessing.
Through faith we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, a New Testament fulfillment of the blessing of peace.
God's peace that surpasses all understanding will guard hearts, an elaboration of the shalom blessing in the New Testament.
Paul asks that the Lord of peace himself may give the church peace, an apostolic continuation of the blessing.
